title: Week of Nov 23
text: Written Nov 16 from LinkedIn and Instagram posts published Nov 2 to 15 (Supermetrics, through Nov 15): 28 LinkedIn posts, the last on Nov 12, and 28 Instagram posts, the last on Nov 13. Compared with Oct 5 to Nov 1 and with October. Series and partners come from the ATM Kitchen board, refreshed Nov 16; Instagram collab status for October posts comes from Instagram, read Nov 12. The Nov 9 briefing did not run, so the tests set on Nov 2 are read here. This week's two experiments run Nov 18 to 25.

title: After the Awards, LinkedIn reach halved, and the winner thank-you cuts that filled the feed drew little on either platform.
text: LinkedIn drew 10,347 impressions Nov 9 to 15, half the 20,722 of Nov 2 to 8 and below the weekly average of 13,842 for Oct 5 to Nov 1; new followers fell from 38 to 22. Seven of the 15 LinkedIn posts Nov 9 to 12 were winner thank-you cuts ("We're thrilled to hand you the M"), with a median of 323 impressions, while the three Awards recaps of Nov 6 drew 1,375 to 2,235. On Instagram the seven winner reels of Nov 9 to 13 reached a median 265, against 1,480 to 3,466 for the four Awards-night posts of Nov 5 and 6, and 28-day reach slipped from 31,694 (to Nov 9) to 29,590 (to Nov 15). The winner reels named people by first name and tagged no one: "Congratulations, Sara!" reached 265 and "Congratulations, Michelle!" 330, while the October honoree reels that named Sara Fischer and Michelle Crossan-Matos in full and tagged @axios and @sharkninja reached 992 and 772. That is the style guide's rule to name every person in full and tag the person and the company; the Publicis Moment of the Year cut (880 on LinkedIn) was the one thank-you that held up.

title: On LinkedIn, guest cuts that open on a story before the name and title drew five times the median of the person-first formula.
text: The style guide asks LinkedIn first lines to lead with the person: "[Name], [Title] at [Company], says ...". The five guest cuts since Oct 26 that opened on a story instead had a median of 3,490 impressions and 13 comments: Justin Breton ("One day, Justin Breton started the morning with a job offer from Gap Inc.") drew 3,863 on Nov 3, Jill Kelly 3,595, Diana Haussling 3,490 and Colleen Dawe (Experian, "She started in media sales") 2,052. The 34 person-first guest cuts of Oct 7 to Nov 12 had a median of 675 and 1.5 comments, and 4 of 34 passed 2,000; the counter-example is Keri Richardson (CrowdAxis, Oct 26), whose story opener drew 240. Four of the five were Awards honorees, AAF Hall of Achievement inductees or Moment Maker guests, so part of the lift may come from the guest. Instagram points the same way: the four reels Nov 2 to 15 that opened on a career moment reached a median 734, against 377 for the three that opened on a number.

title: Accepted Instagram collabs more than doubled guest reel reach, which answers last week's open question.
text: Instagram's collaborator status for October posts, read Nov 12, shows which of the eight single-guest reels of Oct 26 to Nov 1 were accepted collabs. The five accepted (Alice Ma 1,422, Andrew Almendras 1,105, Amanda Forrester 743, Nayeema Raza 647, Keri Richardson 571) reached a median 743; the three without one (Michelle Crossan-Matos 772, Jill Kelly 302, Diana Haussling 219) reached 302. The October style guide found the same gap across the month: 1,634 average views with an accepted collab, 412 without. Michelle Crossan-Matos's honoree reel is the exception. November collab status is not in the data yet, so it cannot yet show whether the best guest reels of Nov 2 to 15 (Bridget Evans 3,211, Justin Breton 2,144, Kerry Flynn 1,355) were collabs.

title: Alternate story openers and person-first openers on next week's LinkedIn guest cuts.
text: For the LinkedIn guest cuts of Nov 18 to 25 (six or more), write two first lines for each. The story opener puts one moment from the guest's life or career first ("One day, Justin Breton started the morning with a job offer from Gap Inc. and ended the day..."), with the full name, title and company in the next sentence; the other is the person-first line the style guide asks for. Post them alternately, starting with a story opener, and spread honorees, AAF inductees and series guests across both sides. Keep the rest of each post the same, tag the guest and the company on both, and keep a list of which opener each post used.
next_step: Measure: median impressions per opener after seven days against 675, the median person-first guest cut Oct 7 to Nov 12 (3,490, the median of five story openers since Oct 26, is the stretch), and median comments against 1.5.

title: Rerun the Instagram hook split: number hooks against career-moment hooks.
text: None of the six guest reels of Nov 9 to 13 opened on a number, so last week's split did not run. For the guest reels of Nov 18 to 25 (four or more), write two hooks for each: one number or fact from the interview, as the style guide asks ("17 schools before she was done moving"), and one career moment ("She got the call about one of the biggest moments of her career while her kids ran wild at a park concert."). Post them alternately, starting with a number hook, and keep the rest of the caption the same. Send the collab invite to the guest and the company on every reel, put the accept ask in the live-links email, and log which hook each reel used and whether the collab was accepted.
next_step: Measure: median reach per hook after seven days, both against 396, the median reel Nov 2 to 15; career-moment hooks had a median of 734 (four reels) and number hooks 377 (three reels) in that window. Compare accepted collabs with the rest against 743 and 302 (Oct 26 to Nov 1).
